item.title: Why Traditional Cybersecurity Won’t “Fix” AI
item.description:
Author: Samantha Pearcy
Date: 2025-11-06
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence Security", "Cybersecurity", "AI Risk Management", "Software Testing", "Adaptive Defense"]
Summary:
  • AI failures differ from traditional software bugs.
  • AI vulnerabilities are learned behaviors, not discrete flaws.
  • Traditional cybersecurity tools cannot fully secure AI.
  • AI requires continuous, adaptive defense strategies.
  • Testing must include dynamic red teaming and behavioral monitoring.
  • Security must blend traditional and AI-native approaches.

item.title: Are AI browsers safe? A security and vulnerability analysis of OpenAI Atlas
item.description:
Author: Giskard Team
Date: 2023-09-12
Tags: ["AI Technology", "Cybersecurity", "Web Browsers", "Data Privacy", "Vulnerability Analysis"]
Summary:
  • AI browsers like OpenAI Atlas offer smarter web navigation.
  • The browser uses GPT models and accesses sensitive data.
  • Several security vulnerabilities were found, including data leakage risks.
  • Penetration testing revealed areas needing stronger encryption and sandboxing.
  • Users should be cautious and expect ongoing security improvements.
  • Continuous audits are vital for safe AI browsing.
